properties.rationale: Deferred on Anthony's word, 2026-07-28, with the rest of the reflow workflow review. Accepted and not dropped, and unusually concrete for a parked item: the mechanical half is specified in the requirement and needs no LLM — does every node type and edge type NAMED in a hint exist in the merged schema, and does every relationship a hint asserts have a corresponding edge type declared between those endpoints. Both are answerable from the schema alone and both would have caught the Anchor case, where two hints assert an Anchor-to-DriftEvent DEPENDS_ON with zero instances and no code path, while passing validate_schema.py cleanly. Deferred rather than built because it is coupled to dec:anchor-retire-or-implement: writing the check before deciding whether Anchor is retired, implemented or aliased would either red-light the build on a type about to be removed, or bless prose about to be rewritten. Decide the Anchor question first, then the check has a known-good corpus to run against. Also worth carrying forward: the check must not overreach — whether a hint's ADVICE is good stays a human question, and a linter that pretended otherwise would be the flattering default this design keeps refusing.
